why_these: The interface work of this stage touched: the device testbench and
the public top (rtl/tnca_shell.v), the core's reset list, the
transport and backend interfaces, the runtime's argument upload, the
compile target's platform_binding split, and the TTIR importer.
Everything downstream of those is in scope.

known_open.why: the pinned Triton wheel exports no AxisInfo and the TTGIR coalesce route does not surface its conclusion either. Both routes are recorded in the checker. This stage did not close it and does not claim to.
known_open.why_not_in_scope: it is open in the baseline too, so running it here would measure the same open question twice rather than whether this stage regressed anything.

known_open.why: GRID-03, -04, -05 and -07 are about per-tile launch on the four-tile machine and are honestly NOT RUN.
known_open.why_not_in_scope: open in the baseline; R36-BASE-02 records that this stage's handoff baseline does not depend on the four-tile runtime.

budget.note: Frozen at the start of the stage, from measurements of the existing small tests rather than from a guess about a new platform. R36-BASE-01 checks these against the contract.
budget.accounting: subprocess by subprocess. A checker that reuses one run for several cases counts it once, which is why the conformance suite opens one device per backend rather than one per case.
